summary.headline: Nephrocare Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23.5% YoY to INR303 crore, but adjusted EBITDA margin slipped to 22.7% as international expansion costs rose.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 revenue reached INR585 crore (+24% YoY) with 570 clinics across six countries after entering Kazakhstan and starting a Saudi clinic. Adjusted EBITDA for H1 was INR134-135 crore at a 23% margin, versus 23.8% for FY26, with management attributing the about 80 bp decline to higher other expenses tied to new-country investment, listed-company costs and ECL provisioning. Adjusted PAT rose 34.7% to INR76.1 crore on lower finance costs after IPO-funded debt repayment. Management reiterated 15-20% medium-term revenue growth guidance and said FY27 capex will exceed INR165 crore.

financial_highlights.value: INR89 crore, about 67% of adjusted EBITDA

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and deposits vs borrowings (30 Sep)

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: 500 clinics across 314 cities (net +13 in H1, gross about 40 added), serving over 33,000 guests, about 80% in tier 2/3 towns. Network utilisation about 74-75%. Growth mainly from PPP contracts in Bihar, Tamil Nadu and Haryana this quarter, with captive additions steady.

segments.name: Philippines
segments.commentary: 55+ clinics after adding 11 in the year, including 10 acquisitions in H1; now second-largest network in the market of around 900 clinics. Management plans 10-15 clinic additions a year and says a greenfield strategy is starting.

segments.name: Uzbekistan
segments.commentary: Six clinics in three provinces serving over 1,450 guests; Tashkent 165-bed clinic described as the largest in the world; business stable. Som currency appreciated about 10% versus INR, and a 5% price increase was taken.

segments.name: Kazakhstan
segments.commentary: Entered this quarter via two acquired clinics in Almaty; market has about 12,000 patients across 150 clinics with universal coverage at roughly $75-80 per treatment. Management expects about a year to reach steady-state margins.

segments.name: Saudi Arabia
segments.commentary: First Riyadh clinic operational; home dialysis started in Riyadh and Jeddah (about 20 patients, half on home care). Operates through a 51%-owned JV, shown below EBITDA. Investment phase until Ministry of Health tender results; bids due February 2027, covering about 11,720 patients in four clusters, with 12 technically qualified bidders.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term revenue growth guidance of 15-20% CAGR over three to four years reiterated; no annual guidance given.
FY27 capital deployment expected to exceed FY26's INR165 crore; INR102 crore already spent in H1.
India addition target of 40-50 clinics a year reiterated; management said BD happens in chunks and could be slightly above 50.
Philippines: management does not expect price increases in the next two to three years, as the last hike was about two years ago.
Saudi capex, if the tender is won, falls in the next financial year (FY28), per management.
Margins are expected to remain in a healthy range, with current level around 23%; new-country launches will cause periodic fluctuation.

qa_highlights.question: Is Indian dialysis tendering moving to QCBS (quality and cost) rather than L1 price-only, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikram Vuppala said NHSRC recommended QCBS to states; states decide, so tenders remain a mix of QCBS and L1, but more tenders are QCBS than five years ago, improving win probability.

qa_highlights.question: Why has margin expansion been limited despite a rising international mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Prashant Goenka said FY26 margin of 23.8% vs H1 FY27 23.0% is the right comparison (about 80 bp down). COGS fell 95 bp to 22% and professional fees fell 83 bp to 18.4%, while other expenses rose from 18.2% to 20% on new-country investment, listed-company costs and model-based ECL.

qa_highlights.question: Are the India and Philippines price points or mix driving the 97% non-forex revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Prashant said the pricing part is largely international mix; management declined to give country-level price or per-treatment figures.

qa_highlights.question: How much of India growth is new clinics versus ramp-up of existing clinics, and how long do new clinics take to stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit Singh said network utilisation is about 75%, growth is about 80-20 from clinic additions, acquired/captive clinics stabilise in 3-6 months, and greenfield clinics in Philippines take 18-24 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the India clinic addition outlook for H2 given 32 net and 40 gross additions in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikram Vuppala reiterated 40-50 clinics a year, said BD comes in chunks and could be slightly above 50; Prashant stressed the 15-20% revenue CAGR as the focus.

qa_highlights.question: Will Saudi tender win drive capex and what is the Saudi JV accounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit said any capex from a win falls in FY28; the 51% JV is shown as a single line below EBITDA (H1 share of loss INR7.5 crore) and not consolidated line by line.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex for the rest of the year and the next two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Prashant said FY27 capex will exceed FY26's INR165 crore, with INR102 crore already spent in H1, and gave no precise figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is Philippines pricing likely to rise over the next two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no price increase is foreseen, as the last hike was about two years ago, though it cannot rule out unknown factors.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the exchange difference in OCI about INR9.88 billion, and when does it recycle to P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: Prashant said it likely relates to unrealisable foreign investments held long term, and the company would respond through the IR mailbox.

capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex deployed about INR102 crore; management expects FY27 capital deployment to exceed FY26's INR165 crore, without giving a precise figure.
Overall network capacity utilisation about 74-75% (India ~75%); first two shifts well occupied, third shift (ending 10 PM) less used, so improvement expected to be marginal.
Saudi capex, if the MOH tender is won, falls in FY28 (next financial year); Saudi is considerably more capex-heavy than India, with no per-bed or per-machine capex disclosed.

Greenfield clinics take about 18-24 months to stabilise on volume; brownfield/captive or acquired clinics stabilise in about 3-6 months; acquired India clinics about 5-6 months, Bihar PPP greenfields 2-3 months.
Dialysis machines depreciated over about 10 years; dialyzers are consumables and not depreciated.
demand_pricing: Q2 revenue INR303 crore (+23.5% YoY, +7.7% QoQ); H1 revenue INR585 crore (+23.6% YoY); treatments grew 12% in Q2; guests 38,814 (+10% YoY).
Revenue per treatment INR2,785, up 9.7% YoY for H1, driven mainly by international mix (about 47% of revenue vs 42% in FY26).
Forex contributed about 3% of Q2 revenue growth (mostly Som, which appreciated about 10% vs INR); 97% from organic, inorganic and price factors. Uzbekistan took a 5% price increase.

India: growth in the quarter driven largely by PPP contracts in Bihar, Tamil Nadu and Haryana (six clinics); PPP is lumpy while captive additions are steady. Management says ~80% of growth comes from clinic additions rather than ramp-up of existing clinics.

Philippines: no price increase expected in the next two to three years, as the last hike was about two years ago. Competition rising from international entrants and local operators, with ~900-clinic market and a 500-plus long tail of single-owner clinics.
Dialyzer pricing expected stable; domestic manufacturing additions may cause slight reduction. Pharmacy products are under 1% of revenue, so proposed trade margin caps are not expected to matter.

Saudi: two large players (Diaverum and a local operator) reportedly hold about 60-65% of the market; the MOH tender covers about 11,720 patients in four clusters with 12 technically qualified bidders.
risks_watch: Saudi MOH tender: bids due February 2027, evaluation about 4-6 months; binary outcome with 12 qualified bidders; management gave no success probability.

Margin trajectory: H1 adjusted EBITDA margin 23% vs 23.8% in FY26; management says new-country launches will keep margins fluctuating, with Kazakhstan ramp-up expected to take about a year to steady state.
Competition in Philippines from new international entrants and local operators as the market consolidates.
Lumpy PPP-driven India additions; BD cycles may cause quarterly volatility in clinic additions versus the 40-50 a year guidance.
Dialyzer prices may ease as domestic manufacturing expands; PVC/oil price shocks could change this.
Uzbekistan Som currency moves and FX affecting reported revenue; forex contributed about 3% of Q2 growth.
Unexplained OCI item (exchange difference on foreign operations, about INR9.88 billion) pending IR follow-up.
key_quotes: Dialysis business is all about scaling up volume.
The margin moderation is investment in future growth and not weaker unit economics.
While we are doing everything we can to improve the chances of winning this tender, of winning a region, by no means we can assure you that we will be one of the winners in this process.
Our primary focus is to grow the revenue by 15% to 20% on a three, four-year basis.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the India platform, volume growth and the 15-20% medium-term revenue guidance, but cautious on near-term margins, which management says will fluctuate as new countries launch. Guarded on Saudi, stressing a binary, uncertain tender outcome and declining to give country-level pricing, capex per bed or success odds.
